scenes.heading: Why atoms share electrons
scenes.narration: Atoms rarely sit alone. When two of them meet they can lock together by sharing electrons, and that sharing explains almost every molecule around you at this very moment.

scenes.heading: Sharing fills the shell
scenes.narration: In a covalent bond neither atom gives an electron away outright. Both contribute, the shared pair counts for each of them, and both partners reach a filled outer shell or octet.

scenes.heading: Comparing with ionic bonding
scenes.narration: Ionic bonding works very differently. In ionic bonding a metal transfers its electrons to a nonmetal outright, and the resulting charged particles stack into a rigid lattice instead.

scenes.heading: Hybridisation of the orbitals
scenes.narration: The molecular orbitals of the two atoms mix together in a process called hybridisation, and these hybrid molecular orbitals then determine the angles that we observe between the bonds.

scenes.heading: Sharing for stability
scenes.narration: So atoms form covalent bonds by sharing electrons to complete an outer shell, reaching a lower energy and more stable arrangement than the two separate atoms could ever manage.

points: Shared pairs fill the outer shell
